ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a voltage-divider biased common-emitter amplifier circuit. The base is formed into voltage-divider bias by Rb1 above and Rb2 below; the collector is connected to +VCC through Rc; the emitter is grounded through Re, and has bypass capacitor Ce; the input terminal is connected to the base through coupling capacitor C1, and the output terminal is connected to load RL through coupling capacitor C2. Reasoning: When finding the quiescent operating point, C1, C2, and Ce are all regarded as open circuits for direct current, so RL does not participate in the direct-current calculation. The base direct-current voltage is approximately determined by the voltage divider: VB = VCC * Rb2 / (Rb1 + Rb2) = 12 * 5 / (15 + 5) = 3.0 V. Given UBEQ = 0.7 V, the emitter voltage VE = VB - UBEQ = 3.0 - 0.7 = 2.3 V. The emitter current IE = VE / Re = 2.3 V / 2.3 kΩ = 1 mA. Approximately take IC ≈ IE = 1 mA. The collector voltage VC = VCC - IC Rc = 12 V - 1 mA * 3 kΩ = 9 V. Therefore the quiescent collector-emitter voltage UCEQ = VC - VE = 9 - 2.3 = 6.7 V.
